categories.main_business_segments: Uoriki Co., Ltd. operates three main business segments: retail, restaurant, and wholesale. The retail segment, which is the core business, sells fresh fish and sushi primarily through tenant stores in metropolitan area train stations, department stores, and supermarkets. The restaurant segment operates sushi restaurants, seafood izakayas, and other seafood-focused dining establishments. The wholesale segment supplies products to supermarkets, regional wholesalers, restaurants, and domestic and international trading companies.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes procurement and logistics capabilities, sourcing fresh fish directly from both the Toyosu Market and production areas, and maintaining freshness through an integrated chilled and frozen logistics network. It employs HACCP-based hygiene management and utilizes ozone sterilization and regular sanitation inspections to ensure food safety. Sushi and seafood products are prepared using in-house expertise in processing and value-added product development, with a focus on freshness and seasonal variety.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include general consumers (via retail stores), supermarkets, regional wholesalers, restaurants, and trading companies. The end markets are mainly the Japanese domestic consumer market, with growing exposure to overseas markets such as Thailand through joint ventures and, to a lesser extent, the United States. The company also targets inbound tourists through its restaurant business.
categories.geographic_coverage: Uoriki's main operations are concentrated in the Tokyo metropolitan area (Kanto region), with additional presence in Kyushu (through the acquisition of Mogami Sengyo) and some activities in the Chubu region. Internationally, the company has a joint venture in Thailand (CP-Uoriki Co., Ltd.) and previously operated in the United States, though US operations are currently suspended.
categories.supply_chain_position: Uoriki operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the seafood supply chain. It procures seafood from upstream producers and wholesalers, processes and distributes products, and sells directly to end consumers through retail and restaurant channels, as well as to other businesses via wholesale.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening the core retail business, expanding overseas, enhancing procurement and logistics efficiency, and building an optimal store portfolio. The company is focused on developing value-added products, especially sushi, and responding to changing consumer needs for convenience and health. It is also investing in sustainability initiatives, such as partnerships with aquaculture firms and climate change risk management, but does not have significant traditional R&D activities.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through direct sales of fresh fish, sushi, and prepared seafood products to consumers (retail and restaurant) and through B2B sales to supermarkets, wholesalers, and restaurants (wholesale). The company also receives some revenue from tenant business operations and minor other sources.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Uoriki positions itself as a leading specialty seafood retailer and sushi provider in the Tokyo metropolitan area, with a growing presence in Kyushu and Southeast Asia. Key competitors include supermarket chains, convenience stores, online retailers, and other specialty seafood retailers. The company differentiates itself through its procurement strength, freshness, and value-added offerings.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were approximately 36.6 billion yen, with operating profit of 1.49 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 1.43 billion yen. The company has shown stable sales growth (0.8% YoY), with a strong balance sheet (equity ratio over 76%) and a recent increase in scale due to the acquisition of Mogami Sengyo. Cash flow is robust, and the company maintains a conservative financial profile.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Uoriki emphasizes delivering high-quality, fresh seafood and sushi at reasonable prices, leveraging its strong procurement network and logistics to ensure freshness and variety. The company highlights its expertise as a specialty fish retailer, its ability to offer seasonal and value-added products, and its commitment to food safety and sustainability. Its differentiation lies in its freshness, product assortment, and customer trust built over decades.
